title: Affine-section dictionary for the resolution flat base-change map
statement: Let f:X→S be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let g:S′→S and g′=pullback.snd g f be flat, and let F be quasi-coherent on X. Take injective resolutions I of F and J of g′*F and an augmentation-preserving lift t:I→g′_*J as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-resolution-construction]. Fix p≥0 and affine opens V⊆S, W⊆S′ with W⊆g⁻¹V. Put A=Γ(S,V), B=Γ(S′,W), with A-algebra structure on B from g.appLE V W, U=f⁻¹V, h=(f.resLE V U) followed by V.toSpecΓ:U→Spec A, and N=F pulled back along U.ι [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then the actual map on sections Γ(W,flatBaseChangeResolutionBeta f g I J t p) is bijective if and only if H.baseChange for h,N,B,p [def-pc-flat-cohomology-comparison] is bijective. The assertion identifies these local maps, without asserting that either is invertible.

proof.text: Restrict the square to affine V in S and affine W in S prime with W contained in g inverse V. The canonical chart isomorphisms identify V with Spec A and W with Spec B, for A=Gamma(S,V), B=Gamma(S prime,W), with ring map g.appLE V W e. The restricted fibre product is U_B for U=f inverse V. Open restriction and iterated pullback identify the coefficient there with N_B for N=F restricted to U. These identifications preserve the coefficient adjunction units, since they are induced by the same pullback square.

Ordinary higher direct images under f and its base change are quasi-coherent by 01XJ. Their higher cohomology on the affine bases vanishes. Apply the cocycle-normalized Leray edge and its vanishing criterion to identify sections of R^p f_*F on V with H^p(U,N), and sections of the base-changed higher image on W with H^p(U_B,N_B). Restriction to an inverse-image open is compatible with this identification, as follows by restricting the same resolution in the cohomology-presheaf description. The affine tensor-pullback section formula then identifies sections of g^*R^pf_*F on W with B tensor_A H^p(U,N). No flat-cohomology base-change isomorphism is used in these identifications.

Use an injective module resolution to compare module cohomology with underlying abelian-sheaf cohomology. Forgotten injectives are acyclic for sections, so both are computed by the same section complex. The comparisons are scalar compatible and preserve the cohomological pullback unit: compute that unit with the augmented lift t on this common complex. The fixed-lift section formula gives that a class xi maps to its cohomological pullback. By B-linearity the corresponding tensor map sends b tensor xi to b times the pullback of xi. This is precisely the canonical H.baseChange, whose definition is the tensor-linear extension of pullback on Ext-based cohomology. Thus the two maps in the statement are conjugate by additive isomorphisms.

Conjugation by bijections preserves and reflects bijectivity, proving the asserted equivalence. This remains valid for p=0, F=0 and U empty; if W is empty then B is the zero ring and both displayed maps are between zero groups.
